32 The current I in a copper wire can be calculated using the equation shown.
I = Anvq
What does the symbol v represent?
A
the average drift velocity of the charge carriers
B
the instantaneous velocity of the charge carriers
C
the voltage applied across the wire
D
the volume of the wire

hints: Look at the other symbols in $I = Anvq$: $A$ is cross-sectional area, $n$ is number of carriers per unit volume, and $q$ is charge per carrier.
Think about how electrons move in copper: fast random motion in all directions plus a very slow net movement along the wire when current flows.
Check the case of the symbol: lower-case $v$ suggests a velocity in $\text{m s}^{-1}$, while voltage and volume use upper-case $V$.
walkthrough: Identify the equation $I = Anvq$ for current in a metal wire, where $A$ is area in $\text{m}^2$, $n$ is carrier number density in $\text{m}^{-3}$ and $q$ is charge in $\text{C}$.
Recall the model: free electrons collide repeatedly with ions, so they move randomly at high speed but gain a small net displacement along the wire due to the electric field.
Define drift velocity as the average velocity of all carriers along the wire direction, which multiplied by $Anq$ gives charge passing per second.
Rule out voltage because it is written $V$ and measured in $\text{V}$, and rule out volume because volume would be $AL$ and written $V$.
Rule out instantaneous velocity because $I$ is a steady average flow, so it depends on the averaged motion, not one electron at one instant.
Therefore $v$ is the average drift velocity of the charge carriers. This is option A.

A.explanation: In $I = Anvq$, $v$ is the mean velocity of electrons along the wire, the drift velocity, typically of order $10^{-4} \text{m s}^{-1}$.

B.explanation: Electrons have very large random instantaneous speeds between collisions, but only their small average motion along the wire contributes to $I$.

C.explanation: Voltage is normally written as $V$, not $v$, and it does not appear in $I = Anvq$ where $q$ is the charge of one carrier.

D.explanation: Volume is $AL$ for a wire of area $A$ and length $L$, so $v$ with lower case cannot represent volume in this equation.
